summary: axios-native impersonates upstream axios with copied source and unrelated publisher
details: Package name 'axios-native' presents itself as axios: package.json description, homepage (axios-http.com), and repository fields point at the real axios project, and dist/node/axios.cjs is a verbatim copy of axios source carrying a header '/*! Axios v1.16.3 Copyright (c) 2026 Jay and contributors */'. The version (1.16.3) and 2026 copyright are ahead of upstream, and the publisher is unrelated to the real axios maintainers. No install/preinstall/postinstall lifecycle scripts fetch or execute remote code, no obfuscated blobs are shipped, and no code path in the copied source has been altered to exfiltrate installer data, contact attacker-controlled hosts, or open a backdoor. The 'ping' string occurrences in dist/node/axios.cjs are part of axios's own timeout/keep-alive code, not a shell invocation. Present risk to an installer is that of a name-lookalike shipping a functional axios copy under a different publisher, which creates a channel for a future release from this account to substitute malicious code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
